clue.text: Allowed a bird to get into bed

indicators.note: one thing getting into another means it goes inside it, so the bird sits within the bed

parts.note: taken as written
a rook is a crow-like bird

explanation.surface: Someone permits a bird to settle into their bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to tolerate or permit it, so brooked is a synonym of allowed.

clue.text: English conductor meets king in an old car

parts.note: Sir Simon Rattle is an English orchestral conductor
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A famous English conductor and a monarch share a vintage motor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattler is an informal name for a rickety old car that rattles as it goes.

clue.text: Like a giraffe, it's all right to have one half pint

parts.note: OK means all right
a means one, as in a single

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the word pint is used

explanation.surface: Permission is given to drink just half a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes PI from 'pint'. The okapi is the giraffe's only living relative.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest animal of the giraffe family, so it is a giraffe-like creature.

clue.text: Busy but still agreed to get married

definitions.meaning: a phone line that is busy is described as in use
a couple who have agreed to marry are betrothed

explanation.surface: A couple are occupied yet have promised to wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaged means both occupied, as of a telephone line, and betrothed to be married.

clue.text: Indirect strike only half completed

parts.note: to knock is to strike or hit

indicators.note: only half of the word only is written out, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A blow that lands only partly, glancing off its target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half completed' is the selection signal: only half of the word 'only' is written. 'Indirect' is an adjective here, as in a knock-on effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A knock-on effect is a secondary, indirect consequence, so the term serves as an adjective meaning indirect.

clue.text: This cardinal was certainly not an old woman

definitions.text: This cardinal was certainly not an old woman

parts.words: This cardinal was certainly not an old woman
parts.note: the phrase 'not an old woman' is read as a modern man, the opposite of an old woman, naming a nineteenth-century English cardinal

explanation.surface: A churchman described as anything but fussy and elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: John Henry Newman was an English cardinal, made a saint in 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: John Henry Newman was a Victorian English churchman who became a Roman Catholic cardinal.

clue.text: Maybe king or queen needs food without substance

parts.note: a king or queen is an example of a playing card
board is food served, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A monarch needs meals that are not filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardboard characters are flat and lifeless, lacking substance or depth.

clue.text: She loves "The Prince", but after work he's endlessly a deceiver

indicators.note: after means the pronoun follows the work abbreviation

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
the pronoun gives its letters, the possessive adding none

indicators.note: endlessly means the deceiver word loses its final letter

parts.note: a liar is a deceiver

explanation.surface: A woman adores her prince, though he turns out to be a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet, Ophelia loves Prince Hamlet. 'endlessly' trims LIAR to LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia is the young woman in Shakespeare's Hamlet who loves the Prince of Denmark.

clue.text: Naps killed cat, excited by amorous activity

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters of these three words are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat dies after being roused from its naps by lovers' horseplay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges NAPS KILLED CAT into the British phrase for playful kissing and cuddling.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap and tickle is British slang for light-hearted sexual play, amorous activity.

clue.text: Volcano to be seen before going back

indicators.note: going back means the word for before is read from right to left

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room

explanation.surface: A volcano you must visit before heading home.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, so it is an example of a volcano.

clue.text: Not a nice woman turned reputable novelist

indicators.note: turned means the insulting word for a woman is flipped round end to end

parts.note: slag is a coarse British insult for a promiscuous woman
worthy means deserving respect, reputable

explanation.surface: A disreputable woman reforms and becomes a respected writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' flips the insult end to end. John Galsworthy wrote The Forsyte Saga.
explanation.definitionFit: John Galsworthy was an English novelist and Nobel laureate, author of The Forsyte Saga.

clue.text: Brief binge around the end of the day

indicators.note: around means the spree word wraps about the final letter

parts.note: a fling is a short spell of wild indulgence, a binge

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A short spree that lasts until the day is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of' picks Y from 'day', which 'around' puts inside FLING.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying visit is a very short one, so flying can mean brief or hasty.

clue.text: Ad for tablet ably modified and swallowed

indicators.note: swallowed means the rearranged letters are taken inside the tablet word

parts.note: a pill is a tablet of medicine

indicators.note: modified means the letters of ably are altered in order

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a pill, cleverly reworded, that patients take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ad' is the definition, not part of the surface's advert; 'modified' reshuffles the four letters, which 'swallowed' tucks inside the tablet word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A playbill is a poster advertising a theatre performance, so it is a kind of advertisement.

clue.text: I'd better be buried by existing head

indicators.note: to be buried by something is to lie inside it, so I'd goes within the existing word

parts.note: present means existing now
the contraction gives the letters as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone warns they had best be laid to rest by the current leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a link word in the surface's idiom 'I'd better'; 'be buried by' sets the contraction inside the word for existing.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a state, company or society.

clue.text: Sources upset about old theatre entrance

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes round the old word
upset in a down clue means the sources word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: roots are origins or sources
aged means old

explanation.surface: Origins turned around a former playhouse door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the sources word backwards, giving STOOR, and 'about' wraps it round the word for old after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage door is the theatre entrance used by performers and staff.

clue.text: This heathen hides silver in a container

indicators.note: in means the silver symbol is put within the container word

parts.note: a pan is a cooking container
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An unbeliever keeps silver stashed in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' is a link word in the surface; 'in' places the silver symbol within the container after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan is someone outside the main world religions, a heathen.

clue.text: Fight for junk

explanation.definitionFit: Scrap means both a scuffle and discarded material, two unrelated senses of one word.

clue.text: A hundred jumped like frogs, cut by repeated blows

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
frogs move by hopping, so this is hopped

explanation.surface: A hundred frogs leap about while someone hacks away.
explanation.definitionFit: To chop is to cut with repeated strokes of a blade, so chopped matches.

clue.text: They're here, being inexperienced in the ATS

indicators.note: in means the inexperienced word sits inside the service initials

parts.note: the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army corps of the Second World War
tender years are young, inexperienced ones

explanation.surface: Young recruits newly present in the women's wartime army.
explanation.walkthrough: The ATS was the British women's army branch in the Second World War; 'in' sets the inexperienced word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Attenders are people who are present at something, so they are the ones who are here.

clue.text: Poet who makes me snore

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: A poet whose verse sends the reader to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges ME SNORE. Ralph Waldo Emerson was a US essayist and poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a nineteenth-century American poet and essayist.

clue.text: Aggressive reporters stand around broken tap

indicators.note: around means the stand word surrounds the rearranged letters

parts.note: a rack is a stand for holding things

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of tap are smashed and reordered

explanation.surface: Pushy journalists gather round a faulty faucet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the letters into TPA, which 'around' sets inside the stand word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat pack is a group of pushy, aggressive journalists or paparazzi.

clue.text: Inactivity? Just sat about with little sister

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of sat are moved around

parts.note: sis is a short, familiar word for sister

explanation.surface: Someone simply sat around with their kid sister doing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SAT into STA; 'Just' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of stillness with no change, inactivity.

clue.text: Family party gets me endless criticism

parts.note: a do is a party or social event

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the criticism word is dropped

parts.note: stick is informal British for harsh criticism, as in getting stick

explanation.surface: A family gathering where one person gets constant criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes K from STICK, British slang for criticism, leaving STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic describes the household and family, as in domestic life.

clue.text: Mistakes made by a scoundrel in time

indicators.note: in means the scoundrel word is placed inside the time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a contemptible person, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: Errors committed by a rogue during some period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' is a link; 'in' sets the scoundrel within the time word, between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are errors, especially a list of printing mistakes, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Composer's journey doesn't start

indicators.note: doesn't start means the journey word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to travel is to make a journey

explanation.surface: A composer's trip fails to get under way.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('is'); 'doesn't start' removes T.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Ravel was a French composer, known for Bolero.

clue.text: Purgative poems about sailors

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of poems are moved around

parts.note: salts, as in old salts, are sailors

explanation.surface: A laxative made of verses on seafarers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges POEMS into EPSOM, the Surrey town that gave the salts their name.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom salts are magnesium sulphate, used as a laxative, which is a purgative.

clue.text: One caught in the loo turning round for a bottle

indicators.note: caught in means the numeral is trapped inside the reversed word
turning round means the toilet word is read backwards

parts.note: lav, short for lavatory, is another word for the loo
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in the toilet spins round looking for a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning round' reverses LAV to VAL, and 'caught in' places I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass container for liquids, a little bottle.

clue.text: Home, so a daughter wants to slip into something

parts.note: d is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees
a dress is something a person slips into

explanation.surface: Back home, a daughter wants to change into something comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is where someone lives, their home.

clue.text: Different girl, one in Italy, to approve of

parts.note: Una is a girl's name, and una is also the Italian word for one
to like something is to approve of it

explanation.surface: A distinctive Italian girl wins someone's approval.
explanation.walkthrough: UNA is clued both as a girl's name and as Italian for one, a doubled hint for the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unalike means not alike, so it is a synonym for different.
